paper.title: Problem-Complexity Adaptive Model Selection for Stochastic Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: K armed mixture MAB (stochastic contextual bandit with arm biases)
unmapped: Each arm i has an unknown bias mu_i in [-1,1] added to <alpha_{i,t}, theta*>
Per-arm context vectors drawn independently with zero conditional mean and conditional covariance >= rho_min I
No upper bound on ||theta*|| is known; regret adapts to ||theta*||
the learner knows rho_min (used in T_min and confidence radius)
settings.definition_quote: The reward for playing arm $i$ at time $t$ is given by, $g_{i,t} = \mu_i + \langle \alpha_{i,t}, \theta^* \rangle + \eta_{i,t}$, where $\{\eta_{i,t}\}_{t=1}^T$ are i.i.d zero mean and $\sigma$ sub-Gaussian noise. The context vector satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\alpha_{i,t}|...] = 0$, and $\mathbb{E}[\alpha_{i,t}\alpha_{i,t}^\top|...] \succcurlyeq \rho_{\min}\, I$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit with unknown sparsity (continuum armed)
unmapped: Sparsity level d* of theta* is unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote: a continuum collection of arms denoted by the set $\mathcal{A}:= \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d:\|x\| \leq 1\}$ Thus, the mean reward from any arm $x \in \mathcal{A}$ is $ \langle x,\theta^* \rangle $, where $\|\theta^*\| \leq 1$. We assume that $\theta^*$ is $d^* \leq d$ sparse, where $d^*$ is apriori unknown to the algorithm.

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-armed contextual linear bandit with nested feature maps (dimension model selection)
unmapped: Nested feature maps phi^1,...,phi^M of dimensions d_1<...<d_M=d known to the learner; theta* has exactly its first d_{m*} coordinates non-zero, with d_{m*} unknown
Feature vectors phi^M(x,a) are sub-Gaussian with known parameter tau^2; lambda_min(Sigma_M) > 0
settings.definition_quote: At each time $t \in [T]$, the forecaster is shown a context $X_t \in \mathcal{X}$... The set of contexts $(X_t)_{t=1}^T$ are i.i.d. with $X_t \sim \mathcal{D}$, a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$ that is known to the forecaster. ... The forecaster then receives a reward $Y_t := \langle \theta^*, \phi^M(X_t,A_t) \rangle + \eta_t$.

algorithms.name: ALB-Dim (Adaptive Linear Bandit - Dimension, with OFUL)

symbols.theta_norm: ||theta*||, Euclidean norm of the unknown parameter
symbols.delta_1: confidence parameter of the first epoch

conditions: contexts have zero conditional mean and conditional covariance >= rho_min I
tuning: T_1 > max{T_min(delta,T), C_1 (max{p,q} b_1)^2 d}, C_1 > 9, T_min = (16/rho_min^2 + 8/(3 rho_min)) log(2dT/delta)

source.label: thm:regret_norm_based
source.quote: Suppose $T_1 > \max\{T_{\min}(\delta,T), C_1 \left ( \max\{p,q\}  \, b_1 \right)^2 \, d \}$, where $C_1 > 9$ ... Then, with probability at least $1-18\delta_1 -\delta_s$, we have R(T) \leq  C_1 (2\tau + K) \|\theta^*\| + C( \|\theta^*\| + 1) (\sqrt{K} + \sqrt{d}) \, \sqrt{T} \, \log (K T_1/\delta_1 ) \log (T/T_1).

results.notes: Holds w.p. >= 1-18 delta_1 - delta_s. Universal constants C, C_1 unspecified, so recorded with O notation. Remark 3: with theta*=0 and K>d, gives O(sqrt(KT)). Regret defined via means per round (pseudo-regret type) but stated with high probability.

symbols.gamma_min: minimum magnitude of a non-zero coordinate of theta*
symbols.T_0: initial phase length set by Equation (T_0 defn), O(d^2 ln^2(1/delta))

source.label: thm:adaptive_dimension
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm \ref{algo:main_algo_dimensions_unknown} is run with input parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $T_0$ as given in Equation (\ref{eqn:T_0_defn}), then with probability at-least $1-\delta$, the regret after a total of $T$ arm-pulls satisfies R_T \leq \frac{50}{{\gamma^{4.65}}}T_0 + 25 \sqrt{T} [ ... ].

results.notes: Probability at least 1-delta. d* mapped to s_sparse. Algorithm does not use T as input, so anytime.

symbols.gamma_min: minimum magnitude of a non-zero coordinate of theta*

source.label: cor:dimension_adaptation
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm \ref{algo:main_algo_dimensions_unknown} is run with input parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $T_0 = \widetilde{O} \left(d^2\ln^2 \left( \frac{1}{\delta} \right) \right)$ ..., then with probability at-least $1-\delta$, the regret after $T$ times satisfies R_T \leq O ( \frac{d^2}{{\gamma^{4.65}}} \ln^2 ( d/\delta) )  + \widetilde{O} ( d^* \sqrt{ T}).

results.notes: First term is O, second O-tilde; recorded combined with O_tilde. Probability >= 1-delta.

symbols.gamma_min: minimum magnitude of a non-zero coordinate of theta*
symbols.T_0: initial phase length from Equation (eqn:T_0_defn_foster), O(d^2 ln^2(1/delta) tau^2 ln(TK/delta))
symbols.d_mstar: true (unknown) dimension d_{m*} of the nested model

conditions: phi^M(x,a) sub-Gaussian with known parameter tau^2
tuning: SupLinRel with feature scaling b(delta) = O(tau sqrt(log(TK/delta)))

source.label: thm:adaptive_dimension_foster
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm \ref{algo:main_algo_dimensions_foster} is run with input parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $T_0$ as given in Equation (\ref{eqn:T_0_defn_foster}), then with probability at-least $1-\delta$, the regret after a total of $T$ arm-pulls satisfies R_T \leq 2T_0 \max \left( 25^4, \frac{2}{{\gamma^{4.65}}} \right) + 308 (1 + \ln(2K T \ln T))^{3/2} \sqrt{T d_{m^*}} + 100 \sqrt{T}.

results.notes: Regret is defined in expectation in the setup but the theorem is stated w.p. >= 1-delta; recorded as high probability. Requires T through b(delta) and T_0.

symbols.gamma_min: minimum magnitude of a non-zero coordinate of theta*
symbols.tau_sg: sub-Gaussian parameter of the feature vectors phi^M(x,a)

source.label: cor:dimension_adaptation_foster
source.quote: Suppose Algorithm \ref{algo:main_algo_dimensions_foster} is run with input parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$, and $T_0 = \widetilde{O} \left(d^2\ln^2 \left( \frac{1}{\delta} \right) \right)$ ..., then with probability at-least $1-\delta$, the regret after $T$ times satisfies R_T \leq O \left( \frac{d^2}{{\gamma^{4.65}}} \ln^2 ( d/\delta) \tau^2 \ln \left( \frac{TK}{\delta}\right) \right)  + \widetilde{O} (  \sqrt{ T d^*_m})

results.notes: Restated identically as Corollary 4 in the appendix (same label).
